newsitem.title: UK: Colombia touts 49 pct of Bogota power company.
newsitem.headline: Colombia touts 49 pct of Bogota power company.

text.p: Colombia is about to offer a 49 percent stake in integrated power company Empresa Energia de Bogota, Minister of Mines and Energy Rodrigo Villamizara told reporters here on Tuesday.
"We are going to promote the company here in London," said Villamizar. "Once we do this, we will try to place 49 percent of the shares in the company."
He did not give a precise timescale for the sale.

"It will become a holding company with power generation, transmission and distribution elements separated," he told reporters, adding the company would have six million customers and would be worth around $1 billion.

Last month Houston Industries, a subsidiary of Houston Light & Power, paid $535 million for the government's 56.7 percent stake in Empresas de Energia del Pacifico (EPSA,) the leading power company in southwestern Colombia.
"The sale of our power generation assets has been very well received," he said.
Villamizar said his energy-rich country was moving swiftly towards natural gas for power generation,
He said some 80 percent of his country's power currently came from hydro-electric sources. This would fall to 60 percent by 2010 under the current expansion plan.
The rest would be thermal power. Of this, 60-70 percent would be generated by natural gas and the rest by coal, which is produced locally.
